speaker_role: Dartmouth alum (interviewed as part of InGenius Prep's admissions interview series, not an admissions officer)
commercial_incentive: Yes - hosted by InGenius Prep, which references its own blog and supplemental-essay help resources at the end
key_insights: Speaker applied to 8-10 schools total, narrowing her list around valuing small liberal arts curriculum flexibility, Northeast location, and a strong campus feel
Applied to some safety schools with rolling admission and heard back by mid-October, which she says relieved stress and let her focus remaining effort on regular decision applications
Describes taking classes across many departments (8 of 9 freshman-year classes in different departments) before settling on a geography major, illustrating exploration-then-focus as a viable path
Notes Dartmouth's D-Plan quarter system means only 3 classes at a time but a faster pace (9-10 week terms) compared to semester schools carrying 4-5 classes
States full-time faculty (not TAs) teaching undergrad classes was a meaningful, underestimated factor in her experience versus what she expected from admissions brochures
Emphasizes campus visits (including an admitted-students day visit) as decisive in her final choice between comparable schools
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker applied to approximately 8-10 schools total
Speaker took 8 of 9 freshman-year classes in different departments before choosing a geography major
notable_or_distinctive: Detailed first-person account of the D-Plan quarter system's practical effect on workload and schedule structure, which is more specific than typical generic 'life at X university' content.
reliability_notes: Single alum's personal narrative, not institutional or current data (published 6 years ago, so some policies like housing/rush timing may have changed); hosted by a paid consulting company promoting its own services at the close.
